messages:
jules: quick noteafter today's kernel-selection fallback landed, canary shows host p99 CPU for short prompts up ~7%
maria: where's the time going?
jules: perf flame (collapsed): parse::tokenize 40%, parse::framer 19%, kvcache::lookup 11%, kernel_select 6%, grpc::small_write 7%, other 17%
cheng: so kernel_select change moved work into preproc and increased fragmentation?
jules: traces show frames/request for <64-token requests increased 1.6x -> 3.1; writev counts doubled; kvcache tail hit-rate down ~1.5%
samir: hypothesis: fallback lowers minibatch ceiling -> framer emits smaller proto slices to prefer latency -> more smallwrites -> syscall/grpc overhead and worse KV locality
maria: mitigation ideas: (1) add hysteresis/hold before switching kernels, (2) coalesce adjacent proto slices in host-preproc within a small time-window, (3) tweak KV admission for small prefixes (needs more sims)
cheng: I'll prototype kernel-hold (hold for N requests or T ms) + minimal coalesce (merge fragments if delta <=1.5ms and size<=8KB). featureflag both
samir: add zap metrics: host.ingress.frames_per_request, host.ingress.writev_per_request, host.kernel.hold_events; sample traces for correlation
maria: gate coalesce on tenant opt-in and smoke test kvcache.hit_rate_drop <=0.5% before wider rollout
jules: plan: rollback fallback on canary now, run canary, then A/B hold+coalesce in next canary. I'll open rollback PR and post canary id here
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: rollback-pr #5201 -> eng-runtime-canary in 7m
jules: thanks team will post perf diffs after canary completes
